$schema_note: THE guardrail file for agent writes in the obot workspace. One per-repo policy, replacing the merge-policy.json + autonomy-grants.json pair (which had to be edited separately for every repo and had already drifted). A repo gets ONE decision: its profile. 'protected' is the default for every repo @jwildfire has not explicitly promoted; 'auto' is a promotion he approves, recorded in the repo's 'approved' block. Anything a repo needs BEYOND its profile goes in 'custom' and needs its own recorded approval. Repos absent from 'repos' are refused entirely - listing a repo is itself a decision. This file sits inside its own carve-out, and since v3 that is mechanical rather than prose: obot-merge reads the PR's changed files, forces the attested lane when they touch a carveOut path, and checks that the copy of this file it is reading matches the 'authority' ref below.

roles._note: Branch ROLES, not branch names - so a repo whose branches are not called dev/main needs no special-casing. Each repo entry maps its own branch names onto these roles; the profile decides what each role permits. A branch with no role is refused outright under every profile.
roles.integration: The lane work lands on: where feature branches merge and where the next release accumulates. One per repo. Usually 'dev', but 'main' where there is no dev (obot.agent, obot.roadmap, demo-301).
roles.release: The published or protected surface - changing it changes what the world sees. Zero or more per repo. A release branch ('main', 'master'), or a published-site source (demo-301's 'site' is the live GitHub Pages branch).

protected._summary: The default. Nothing merges without @jwildfire's explicit in-session approval, attested on the PR; unattended (--auto) sessions may not write to the repo at all. Equivalent to how a repo behaved under the old pair when it was listed for merges but absent from the autonomy matrix - minus the standard merge lane.

autonomy._note: An --auto session selecting an increment in a 'protected' repo must refuse and say so - this repo is outside its grant.

auto._summary: Promoted per repo by @jwildfire. The integration branch merges on the standard lane under the standing operating contract (his approval of the WORK is still required - the lane only removes the mechanical block); release branches still require attestation; unattended sessions may branch, open draft PRs, merge integration, and manage issues.

lanes._note: What the three merge outcomes mean to obot-merge.
lanes.standard: Mergeable via obot-merge with no extra flag. Contract-gated: @jwildfire approved the work; the tool removes the mechanical block, it is not the approval.
lanes.attested: Mergeable ONLY with a recorded approval, posted on the PR as an audit comment before the merge. --jeremy-approved '<where/when he approved>' is his approval of this merge and is always valid. --decision '<what he already decided>' is valid only for a carve-out merge into the integration branch of an 'operational' repo - never for a release-role branch, never for a 'clinical' repo. Never available to an unattended session: there is no in-session approval to attest, and a recorded decision is not a licence to act unattended.
lanes.refused: Not a merge target. obot-merge exits 2.

invariants._note: True under every profile, and independent of a repo's 'class'. A repo entry cannot opt out of these; only @jwildfire can, in session, per merge.
never: merge a release-role branch without @jwildfire's explicit in-session approval, attested via --jeremy-approved

merge any PR touching a carveOut path without @jwildfire's explicit sign-off, attested via --jeremy-approved - on any lane, in any repo, attended or not (@jwildfire, 2026-08-15, decision D0005.1/W1). Unattended sessions therefore cannot merge one at all: there is no in-session approval to attest.
tag or publish a release (prep is allowed: notes draft + staged promotion PR)
delete anything - files, issues, branches, releases, history - without approval
write to any repo outside the jwildfire org: read-only, no exceptions, drafts handed to @jwildfire
merge into a branch with no role in this file

autonomy._note: Global dials for --auto sessions, unchanged from autonomy-grants.json. These gate the whole run; the per-repo profile gates each write. Effective unattended merge = profile 'auto' AND role 'integration' AND level != A0 AND no carveOut path touched.

levels.A0: observed runs - draft-PR-only, no merges anywhere except the obot.roadmap standing grant (demotion target)
levels.A1: routine merges - standard-lane obot-merge unattended, minus the carve-out; the attested lane never (entry level, decided 2026-07-22)
levels.A2: scheduled - nightly trigger without a human launch (not yet enabled)

budgets._note: checked at phase boundaries; hitting a cap parks the increment with a digest

issueCloses.except: hub Requirement issues - those close via release promotion PRs that @jwildfire approves
issueCloses.requires: verifiable completion (merged PR by headRefOid, or directly verified repo state) cited in the closing comment

releases._note: notes draft + staged promotion PR allowed; tagging and publishing always human-triggered

autonomy.outsideOrg: read-only, no exceptions - drafts handed to @jwildfire

carveOut._note: The guardrail files. A PR touching any of these is forced onto the attested lane whatever the repo's profile says, and merges only with a recorded approval from @jwildfire (@jwildfire, 2026-08-15, D0005.1/W1: 'always require the flag'). Two forms count, and the tool tells them apart: --jeremy-approved '<where/when he said so>' is his approval of THIS merge, and is the only form accepted on a release-role branch or in a 'clinical' repo; --decision '<artifact/issue + what it decided>' cites a decision he already recorded, and is accepted only on the integration branch of an 'operational' repo - the case where he has ruled that routine work is the agents' to land and must not come back to him (his correction, 2026-08-15: 'this isnt an RC or an artifact'). Neither form is available to an unattended session. Keys are repos; a path ending in '/' matches by prefix, anything else matches exactly; no globs, case-sensitive, repo-root-relative, and a rename counts as a touch on both its old and new path. The list is the permission surface only - documentation that happens to live beside it is ordinary work (which is why the goal registry is listed by file rather than by its directory).

unversioned._note: Governed surfaces that live outside every git repository, so no PR can touch them and no merge gate can see them. They are enforced through the in-repo sources listed above, and documented here so the mapping is not folklore.
unversioned.workspace .claude/settings.json: hook registrations written by jwildfire/obot.agent hooks/install.sh

classes._note: The operational-vs-clinical control split (@jwildfire, 2026-08-15, decided in obot.roadmap discussion #160 over the artifact at reports/decisions/2026-08-15-operational-clinical-classification/). 'operational' = agents self-improve with automatic merges to production plus periodic releases to a lagging release branch; 'clinical' = @jwildfire reviews everything before it reaches the released surface, and releases are formally documented as soon as they go live. Every repo entry carries a 'class'; obot-policy validate warns on a repo without one. The class records intent - the merge lanes still come from the profile.

approved.where: Q&A #160 answer: open.csr and open.gismo clinical, demo-301 clinical (his override of the operational recommendation), the rest as recommended, class field in policy.json approved

authority._note: The governed copy. obot-merge compares the blob sha of the policy file it just read against this ref before deciding anything; a mismatch means the guardrail under the tool's feet is not the one in force - which is exactly what happens when a session runs obot-merge from a worktree whose branch edits this file - so the attested lane is forced and the mismatch is stated out loud. An unreachable authority forces attested too: an attended session can still merge with the flag, an unattended one cannot merge at all, which is the correct failure direction.
